source_text: Quod si dixeris, quam sis aperte Manichaeus, etiam patroni tui poterunt confiteri. Si vero intellexeris tantum veri Regis exercitum contra tuam dimicare sententiam, nec illis te afferre posse praeiudicium; acquiesce destructum esse quod extruxeras, et per hoc non ire omnes ex uno in condemnationem [n324] ; sed eos tantum, qui rebelles voluntati Dei, sine paenitentia, sine correctione, ultimo fuerint fine deprehensi.
pass_a_gloss: Which if you shall have said, how openly you are a Manichaean, even your patrons will be able to confess. But if you shall have understood so great an army of the true King to fight against your sentence, nor that you can bring a prejudgment to those; acquiesce that what you had built has been destroyed, and through this that not all go from one into condemnation; but those only, who rebellious to the will of God, without repentance, without correction, shall have been caught by the last end.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: If you say this, even your patrons will be able to acknowledge how openly Manichaean you are. But if you recognize so great an army of the true King fighting against your opinion, and realize that you cannot harm their standing, admit that what you built has been destroyed. Consequently, not everyone goes from one into condemnation (Romans 5:16), but only those who, rebellious against God's will, are overtaken by their final end without repentance or correction.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

bible_refs.note: From Pass B Scripture tagging; wording follows Julian's Latin, not a modern Bible.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
